stem: Draw the straight line $2y = x - 4$. Any two points on the line will do; the equation under the graph updates as you drag.
solution: The equation is not yet in the form $y = mx + c$: $y$ has a $2$ in front of it.
Drag the first point onto the $y$-intercept, $(0, -2)$.
Use the gradient: up 1 for every 2 across, so the second point is $(2, -1)$.
notes: Mirrors ex6-2-5a (2y = 3x - 1), with numbers chosen so the true gradient is the reciprocal of a whole number, which the instrument requires (3/2 would be refused). Two ways to skip the division: (1) divide the x-term only, giving y = x/2 - 4, which has the right slope and the wrong intercept, so it fires intercept-wrong; (2) read m = 1 and c = -4 as printed, which matches neither, so it fires off-target. Both are the read-m-before-y-is-alone error. The swapped gradient and intercept (m = -4, c = 1) also fire off-target; the printed-reading error is likelier here because the 2y is the whole point of the question, so off-target maps to it. A student who multiplies by 2 instead of dividing gets slope 2 and would fire slope-inverted; it is left unmapped because no listed misconception names it. The missing-x-term-gradient-one misconception needs a horizontal line (m = 0), which the line_drawer spec does not accept, so it cannot be covered.
